question: Should OpenClaw expose finite cron, webhook, and subagent task completion as a new internal event, or redefine the existing session-end lifecycle contract to cover both task completion and persisted-session retirement?
rationale: A session may remain reusable after an agent turn or subagent task finishes, while the existing plugin `session_end` contract represents retirement or replacement of persisted session state; source inspection cannot determine whether maintainers intend those concepts to be unified.

options.title: Separate completion event
options.body: Keep `session_end` for persisted-session retirement and add a distinctly named internal or plugin event for finite run completion.

options.title: Mirror retirement internally
options.body: Add internal `session:end` only when a persisted session is replaced, reset, compacted, or deleted, leaving task completion to another surface.

options.title: Broaden session end
options.body: Define both internal and plugin session-end events to fire for cron, webhook, and subagent completion as well as persisted-session retirement.

recommendation.title: Separate completion event
recommendation.body: Keep `session_end` for persisted-session retirement and add a distinctly named internal or plugin event for finite run completion.

likelyOwner.reason: This account introduced and repeatedly evolved the internal hook system, giving it the clearest historical connection to the lifecycle contract decision.
